hook_text: Every gearbox makes you a promise and breaks it at the same time: faster, or stronger, pick one.
clip_script: Here is the secret of every gearbox. Gears meet tooth for tooth, so the teeth are steps. A 10-tooth gear takes 10 steps in one turn. Those 10 steps only move a 30-tooth gear a third of the way round. Small driving big: the big one is slow. Swap them. 30 steps spin the 10-tooth gear three times. Big driving small: the small one is fast. That is your bicycle. Small chainring, big sprocket, slow wheel, easy hill. Big chainring, small sprocket, fast wheel, flat road. Now the catch. Slow always comes with strong; three times slower is three times the force. Fast always comes with weak. You can have speed or you can have force, and no gear ever built gives both. Pick the one your job needs.
visual_style: Whiteboard pair of gears with tooth counts; a step counter ticks as they turn; the pair swaps sizes and the output arrow lengthens; a bicycle appears with low and high gear highlighted.
pacing: Step-counting demonstration, the swap, the bicycle, the one-line catch.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work out the velocity ratio of a 12-tooth gear driving a 36-tooth gear.
